utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you another question in respect of what you said in paragraph 43. In the camp in Batkovic, you remembered two Muslims who had a special status among the inmate population. Their nicknames were Pike and Spajzer. Why do you remember them so well?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: I remember these two detainees because they were favoured. They had certain privileges that the camp guards gave them. They could eat as much as they wanted, and they could also behave like the Serb soldiers behaved. They could walk into the camp, and they could mistreat and beat whomever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they mistreat you?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else mistreat you personally, physically?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did that happen in Batkovic or outside the facility at Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: In Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many times did this happen, or was this on a single occasion?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it happened once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were hit by a hand.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: A hand, a foot, a rifle-butt. I cannot remember all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross when you arrived in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Not immediately after my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber when the ICRC came after your arrival.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it was six or seven weeks after we were registered. After -- we were registered six or seven weeks after we arrived. Or perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to send mail through the prison administration and the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: When we were registered by the Red Cross, we were given the possibility of writing messages to relatives, friends, anyone we knew, and we were promised that these messages would be delivered to such persons, if such a person could be found in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you avail yourself of that opportunity?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I sent a message to my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of receiving an answer to that message?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Batkovic, did you get meals?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Three meals?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will conclude with a question related to personal hygiene. Did you receive soap and the like?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: The prison administration didn't give us anything. As far as personal hygiene was concerned, we got our first supplies after we were registered by the Red Cross, the International Red Cross, for the first time. These supplies consisted of toothpaste, a tooth-brush, and a small bar of soap.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to conclude with a question that has to do with a man who you knew by the nickname of Spajzer. Did he leave Batkovic before you did?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you remember him so well?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, he enjoyed certain privileges from the soldiers and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been asked. The question has been answered. Please, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, then I'm going to conclude by putting this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were exchanged and you went to Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: I was exchanged and went to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1993?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Together with you, another group of detainees were exchanged from Batkovici. Detainees from Batkovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: The group that I was in included 40 prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The number of prisoners from the moment when you arrived in June 1992 until June 1993 when you were exchanged is the number of -- is actually a number that was considerably lower than the original one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: The number of detainees in Batkovic camp varied because some people left and others were being brought in. I would not say that it was decreased radically.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you have now -- you are now starting your fourth or fifth final question. Last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. With your leave, I will just suggest that this indictment that was used here in the courtroom as MFI'd, I would like to suggest that it be admitted into evidence once it's been translated. I don't have anything else to tender because everything else has already been admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I think it was MFI'd because it was tendered but there was no translation, so that status is there already. Mr. Jeremy, any question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: One question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, at temporary transcript page 88, lines 17 to 23, you were asked about the mixed police/army force headquartered at the farm where you stayed before going onto Susica camp, and you confirmed that they did not mistreat you. Did any members of that unit speak to you about their operations?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And what did they say?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR PASIC
utterances.text: They said that in the territory of the town of Rogatica, they attacked the town and they had a minor incident in which one of them almost lost his life, because they were not careful in terms of where they should shoot in the part of town where they went to cleanse the town of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Bench also has no further questions, Mr. Pasic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. And I would invite you to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then briefly, for the record, the Chamber understands that the portions selected by both parties of P431, MFI'd, has been uploaded as 65 ter 02353A and is therefore ready to be admitted into evidence and will receive - Madam Registrar, please correct me when I'm wrong - P431A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's the 65 ter number, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I gave -- but it will be admitted under number? I think it would receive an A number as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be the same as it was MFI'd. So P431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think P431 is the whole of the 16th Session, whereas, the selected portion which has now been uploaded as 65 ter 2353A would then be admitted into evidence separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then as the number P437, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we cannot work with P431A. If that is impossible, then we have to take care. P437 is admitted into evidence. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume, Monday, the 5th of November, in this same courtroom, I, if I'm not mistaken ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We resume Monday, the 5th of November, at 9.30 in the morning, in Courtroom III. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of November, 2012, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
